detail.longDescription: I have a discriminated union where the relationship between type and payload is preserved when I work directly with the union: type Message = | { type: "text"; payload: string } | { type: "count"; payload: number }; function handle(message: Message) { if (message.type === "text") { message.payload.toUpperCase(); } if (message.type === "count") { message.payload.toFixed(); } } However, when I try to express the same relationship through generics, TypeScript no longer seems to preserve the correlation: type MessageMap = { text: string; count: number; }; function handle<K extends keyof MessageMap>( type: K, payload: MessageMap[K] ) { if (type === "text") { payload.toUpperCase(); } } The call site is type-safe, but inside the generic function type === "text" doesn't narrow payload to string . Why can't TypeScript use the relationship between K and MessageMap[K] for control-flow narrowing? Is there a type design that preserves this correlation without manually converting the generic into a discriminated union?
